text: Port Ansgar will host Kestrelline Rail’s new maintenance depot, the company confirmed on Tuesday after months of speculation along the Harrow Coast. The site, a reclaimed freight yard on the eastern edge of the city, will be converted into a £68 million facility designed to service the operator’s expanding intercity fleet. Kestrelline said construction will begin in March and that the depot should open by late 2027, creating about 240 jobs once fully staffed. City officials have long argued that Port Ansgar’s rail heritage, once centered on dockside marshalling and engine sheds, made it the natural choice. For residents, the project marks another turn in the city’s slow return to its old role as a rail hub.
